the thermodynamic and structural characterization of DNA-protein interactions using equilibrium cyclization of short DNA duplexes.
the thermodynamic properties of the interaction of the histone-like proteins, HU and H-NS, with DNA.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

HU dimers bind to DNA with a high affinity (K(a) > 10(5) M(-1)) and with an orientation in which the DNA is bent by about 30 degrees and the HU dodecamer is aligned with its long axis parallel to the long axis of the DNA.
HU binds with high affinity to curved DNA and with low affinity to linear DNA.

HU binding enhances the extent of equilibrium cyclization of all the duplex DNAs studied and that the enhancement of cyclization is due to a stabilization of the cyclized state of the DNA by HU binding.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the equilibrium cyclization method is a powerful tool for monitoring protein-DNA interactions.
HU binding is a cooperative process with an affinity that is dependent on the DNA sequence and the presence of mismatches.
the binding of HU to DNA is a cooperative process, with a binding affinity that increases with the number of sites available to HU.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the HU dodecamer is a flexible, highly dynamic protein, which is capable of binding to a variety of DNA substrates with a preference for curved, mismatched DNA.
HU is an effective stabilizer of DNA structures that are inherently flexible.
the equilibrium cyclization technique can be used to determine the binding affinity of HU to duplex DNA.
